wiki_text: Adriaports (the sponsor group's own project page) states the investment 'prevede di portare a terra 1 miliardo di metri cubi' (envisions bringing ashore 1 billion cubic meters), 'con la possibilita di triplicare il volume' (with the possibility of tripling the volume) once additional berths are secured. This figure is NOT staged as the terminal's Capacity: the source page gives no time basis (no 'annuo'/per-year qualifier), and it does not visibly reconcile with the only concrete commercial figure reported -- a supply agreement for 'massimi 400 ISO-container' of LNG (also adriaports.com), which is a discrete initial cargo/shipment arrangement, not an obviously annualized throughput. Taking 400 x 40-ft ISO containers at roughly 17-18 t LNG each implies a far smaller volume than 1 billion standard cubic meters of gas; the 1 bcm figure reads more like an aspirational full-build-out target for the whole floating-storage-to-shuttle logistics scheme (assuming many more shuttle runs than the initial 400-container deal covers) than a near-term operating capacity. No independent second source was found that restates or clarifies what the 1 bcm figure specifically measures (vessel throughput vs. multi-year cumulative vs. full-buildout design target). Given the ambiguity -- and given the live database is known to carry at least one existing capacity-basis error at a sister FSU record (Port of Vlora FSRU 2, capacity ~1e9x too large) -- Capacity was left blank for this record rather than staging a number that may be off by orders of magnitude. If a future batch finds a clean, dated, per-year figure, it should replace this note.
